The core empirical findings demonstrate that seq2seq models, when properly aligned with their pretraining objectives and using effective prompt designs, can achieve performance comparable to or even surpassing decoder-only models in few-shot learning tasks. The authors conduct extensive experiments on a variety of tasks, including natural language understanding (NLU) tasks from the SuperGLUE benchmark and generation tasks from the XSum and WebNLG datasets. The results consistently show that the proposed methods significantly improve the few-shot learning ability of seq2seq models. The paper also includes an analysis of the permutation bias of the fusion-based approaches, showing that the order of examples does not significantly affect performance. Overall, this paper makes a valuable contribution by highlighting the potential of seq2seq models for ICL and by proposing practical methods to enhance their few-shot learning capabilities.
